stem.solarsystem.mars_liquid_outer_core_: A liquid iron-rich outer core surrounds the newly detected inner core; why the ancient global dynamo ceased remains modeled
stem.solarsystem.mars_solid_inner_core_i: InSight seismic analysis supports a solid inner core about 600 km in radius
stem.solarsystem.uranus_hot_ice_model: Models include a hot water-ammonia-rich mantle; experiments suggest carbon may form sinking diamonds at depth
stem.solarsystem.neptune_hot_ice_model: Models include a hot water-ammonia-rich mantle; experiments suggest carbon may form sinking diamonds at depth
stem.solarsystem.compare_equal_gravity: Both worlds have the same listed gravity at the displayed precision.
stem.solarsystem.compare_bar_scale_note: Compare the two bars within each chart. The charts have different units and scales; their lengths cannot be compared across charts. Here, 1 g is standard Earth gravity. Giant-planet gravity is listed at a reference atmospheric level, not solid ground.
stem.solarsystem.signal_notebook_method: Keep the destination and signal speed the same. Record A, change only the orbital angle, then record B. What changed in the distance and delay?
stem.solarsystem.signal_shared_time_scal: Both bars share a linear time scale:
stem.solarsystem.signal_notebook_limits: Reply times assume an immediate response and an available signal path. These are model observations, not live measurements.
stem.solarsystem.signal_angle_already_re: This angle is recorded. Move the angle slider to collect a different observation.
stem.solarsystem.signal_record_ready: Ready to record the current setup.
stem.solarsystem.signal_explanation_help: At A, I measured ___. At B, I measured ___. The delay changed because ___. Use Save signal evidence below to keep these readings and your explanation in the journal.
stem.solarsystem.moon_cycle_explanation: Waxing means the visible sunlit portion grows; waning means it shrinks. First and third quarter occur one-quarter and three-quarters through the phase cycle; both show a half-lit disk. Ordinary phases are not caused by Earth’s shadow.
stem.solarsystem.moon_orientation_note: These schematic views rotate the disk, not the phase or illuminated fraction. Its actual angle in the sky depends on your location and the time. The disk shows ordinary phase illumination, not eclipse darkening.
stem.solarsystem.compare_challenge_small: Can the smaller world have stronger gravity?
stem.solarsystem.compare_challenge_simil: Can different sizes have similar gravity?
stem.solarsystem.compare_try_question: Try a question, then look for evidence
stem.solarsystem.compare_reasoning_help: Use two measurements: I notice ___. My evidence is ___ and ___. This supports my claim because ___. You can also discuss your explanation with a partner.
stem.solarsystem.try_another_angle_rever: Try another angle, reverse the route, or name a model limitation.
stem.solarsystem.spacecraft_to_destinati: Spacecraft-to-destination gap in AU across the same flight time. Dashed curve: aligned launch. Solid curve: test launch. Triangle: smallest plotted test gap. Cursor follows the flight controls.
stem.solarsystem.select_world_for_3d_mod: Select a world for the 3D model
stem.solarsystem.scale_walk_twenty_cm_su: With a 20 cm Sun and one physical scale, Earth is about 1.8 mm wide and 21.5 m away; Neptune is about 646 m away. Sizes and distances can share a scale, but tiny worlds are hard to see across such a large space. Try the scale-walk planner to choose your own model size.
stem.solarsystem.great_red_spot_desc: A high-pressure storm at 22 degrees south, wider than Earth and shrinking for a century.
stem.solarsystem.hexagonal_vortex_desc: A six-sided jet stream around the north pole, wider than two Earths.
stem.solarsystem.himalayas_desc: Formed by India colliding with Asia. Still rising ~5 mm/year.
stem.solarsystem.pacific_ocean_desc: Largest ocean, covering a third of Earth's surface.
stem.solarsystem.mid_ocean_ridge_desc: Longest mountain range, where new ocean crust forms.
stem.solarsystem.sahara_desc: Largest hot desert; its dust fertilises the Amazon.
stem.solarsystem.amazon_desc: Largest rainforest, home to a tenth of known species.
stem.solarsystem.olympus_mons_desc: Tallest volcano in the solar system, 21.9 km high and 600 km across.
stem.solarsystem.valles_marineris_desc: A canyon system 4,000 km long and up to 7 km deep.
stem.solarsystem.hellas_planitia_desc: A 2,300 km impact basin, the deepest point on Mars.
stem.solarsystem.syrtis_major_desc: Dark volcanic plain, the first surface feature ever recorded on another planet (1659).
stem.solarsystem.tombaugh_regio_desc: The heart: a 1,000 km basin of nitrogen ice that slowly convects.
stem.solarsystem.cthulhu_macula_desc: Dark equatorial belt coated in reddish tholins made by sunlight on methane.
stem.solarsystem.caloris_basin_desc: A 1,550 km impact basin; the shock sent hills rippling to the far side of the planet.
stem.solarsystem.hokusai_crater_desc: Young rayed crater whose bright ejecta streaks wrap much of the planet.
stem.solarsystem.gas_giant_interior_mode: Gas giants have no solid surface. Gas compresses into dense fluid and electrically conducting metallic hydrogen.
stem.solarsystem.ice_giant_interior_mode: Ice-giant interiors are modeled as gas envelopes over hot water-ammonia-rich mantles and small rocky cores.
stem.solarsystem.pluto_interior_model_co: Pluto likely has a water-ice crust over a rocky core; a buried ocean remains a scientific hypothesis.
stem.solarsystem.rocky_interior_model_co: Rocky worlds have metal-rich cores, rocky mantles, and comparatively thin crusts.
stem.solarsystem.interior_model_disclosu: Evidence-based model — boundaries and thicknesses are approximate and not to scale.
stem.solarsystem.ice_giant_diamond_zone_: Models place high-pressure carbon crystallization thousands of kilometers below the clouds.
Experiments suggest sinking diamond crystals could grow at depth; their size and fate inside Uranus remain uncertain.
stem.solarsystem.ocean_scenery_illustrat: Illustrative ocean habitats, with compressed depths and distances.
stem.solarsystem.gravity_inspect_help: Choose a time to freeze both objects in the shafts above. Both share the same elapsed time. Run the drop again to replay the animation.
stem.solarsystem.gravity_acceleration_ex: Distance fallen = ½ × g × time², starting from rest. At half of its own fall time, an object has fallen one-quarter of the height. It covers more distance in each equal time interval as it speeds up. Positions stop at the drop endpoint; no bounce is modeled.
stem.solarsystem.lifespan_log_axis: log scale · 0.6 Myr (50 M☉) to 3.2 Tyr (0.1 M☉)
